Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:1.english: About the size of an issar - The mouth of the spring from which it flows was as wide as an issar.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:2.hebrew: אל יתהלל חכם - שחכמתו אינה אלא מקלקלת, לפי שכלי מקדש ראשון ע"פ הגבורה נעשו, דכתיב (ד"ה א כח): הכל בכתב מיד ה' עלי השכיל כל מלאכת התבנית:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:2.english: Let not the wise man glory - For his wisdom only spoils [it], because the vessels of the First Temple were made by the word of the Almighty, as it is written (I Chronicles 28:19): "All in writing from the hand of the Lord upon me He made me understand, all the works of the pattern."

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:1.hebrew: הרדווליס טבלא גורגדנא - זוג ועינבל, שקורים אישקליט"א:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:1.english: Hirdavlis, tabla gurgdana - A bell and clapper, which they call eschelette.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:2.english: And disrupts the melody - When this sound would conclude.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:18:1.hebrew: מגריפה - שבה גורפין את דשן המזבח, וודי"ל, והוא כעין כף:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:18:1.english: Magreifa - [That] with which they shovel the ash of the altar; vadil, and it is like a scoop.

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:17:1.hebrew: הרדווליס - בסמ"ך גריס רש"י, ונראה לר' הרדוולים במ"ם. וכן יש בבראשית רבה: "ערדולין בעיר ומדינה נהפכה". פירוש: ערדוולין כמו הרדוולין, והם מיני כלי זמר; מ"ם מתחלפת בנו"ן. הרדוולים — זהו תרגום של עוגב:
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:17:1.english: Hirdavlis - Rashi reads [the text] with a samekh, and it appears to the Rabbi [to read] hirdavlim with a mem. And so it is in Bereishit Rabbah: "An ardulin is in the city, and the province is overturned." Explanation: ardavlin is like hardavlin, and they are types of musical instruments; [and a final] mem interchanges with [a final] nun. Hirdavlim — this is the translation of "ugav" [in the Targum].

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:18:1.hebrew: מגריפה היתה במקדש - פי' בקונטרס שגורפין בה הדשן. וקשה, דהא היתה כלי זמר! אלא נראה לפרש, דשני מיני מגריפות היו: אחת לדשן, ואחת של שיר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:18:1.english: "There was a magreifa in the Temple" - [Rashi] explains in the Kuntres that they would shovel the ashes with it. And this is difficult, for behold, it was a musical instrument! Rather, it appears [correct] to explain that there were two types of magreifot: one for the ashes, and one for song.
